title: Module 5 Quiz: Risk Management in DeFi

questions.text: How does bridge risk differ from smart contract risk on a single blockchain?
options: Bridge risk specifically involves smart contracts that facilitate moving tokens across different blockchains.
Bridge risk only applies to centralized exchanges rather than DeFi protocols.
Bridge risk refers exclusively to governance takeover by whale wallets.
Bridge risk occurs when stablecoins lose their parity with pegged fiat currencies.
questions.explanation: Bridge risk specifically targets the cross-chain smart contracts used to transfer tokens between distinct blockchain networks.

questions.text: What is the primary security benefit of using separate hot burner wallets for testing new protocols?
options: Burner wallets automatically revoke contract permissions after every transaction.
Burner wallets guarantee protection against token de-pegging and economic risks.
It isolates high-risk interactions so a compromised signature cannot access your main asset stash.
Burner wallets eliminate the need to inspect contract addresses during signing.
questions.explanation: Hot burner wallets restrict potential losses to small test balances, keeping your main vault isolated from malicious signatures.

questions.text: True or false: Setting a custom token allowance cap instead of granting unlimited approval helps limit potential loss during a contract exploit.
questions.explanation: Custom allowance caps restrict smart contract access to a specific number of tokens rather than your complete balance.

questions.text: True or false: A crypto rug-pull happens when developers remove underlying liquidity from a trading pool, rendering the token worthless.
questions.explanation: A rug-pull occurs when developers pull the liquidity backing a token, leaving investors with untradeable, worthless tokens.
